info.desc: Elvis Presley (released in the UK as Elvis Presley Rock n' Roll) is the debut album by American rock and roll singer Elvis Presley. It was released on RCA Victor, catalog number LPM-1254, in March 1956. The recording sessions took place on January 10 and January 11 at the RCA Victor recording studios in Nashville, Tennessee, and on January 30 and January 31 at the RCA Victor studios in New York. Additional material originated from sessions at Sun Studio in Memphis, Tennessee, on July 5, August 19 and September 10 of 1954, and on July 11, 1955. The album spent .

podcast.body: Elvis Presley's inaugural album featured his cover version of Carl Perkins's "Blue Suede Shoes" as its opening track. This was part of a "gentleman's agreement" to delay the single release of Elvis's version, thereby protecting the sales of Perkins's original. podcast.body: Recorded after the "Heartbreak Hotel" sessions, consisting mostly of R&B and Rockabilly covers. The material was almost entirely Elvis's own choice, resulting in "fine performances and perfect for album tracks." "Almost all of these were Elvis's own choice of material, and so while his versions of Blue Swade's shoes, or Tuti Fruity, didn't match the quality of the originals, they were fine performances and perfect for album tracks."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.body: The self-titled album features a cover shot of Elvis Presley playing guitar. Its layout and typography significantly influenced The Clash's artwork for their album "London Calling." "His self-titled 1956 album featured a shot of him playing guitar. And as on the side here, some of the layout and topography of that record was used by the clash for the aforementioned London Calling artwork."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
